Notice of Hearing 
The Department of Natural Resources announces that it will hold a public hearing on a 
permanent rule to revise chs. NR 12, 16, 19, 21, 22, 27, 40 and 45 relating to amphibian and 
reptile regulations, at the time and place shown below. 
Hearing Information 
Date:  January 12, 2026 
Time:  5:00 p.m.  
Virtual Location Link: Join the meeting now 
   
Rule Information: Current rules establish provisions for a variety of activities involving 
Wisconsin’s native amphibians and reptiles, including harvest, live take, possession, 
propagation, purchase, sale, trade, exhibition, rehabilitation, stocking and release. However, the 
majority of these rules have not been updated since the 1990s. Additionally, the department has 
heard feedback that these rules are difficult to interpret and enforce. These rules will be updated 
to provide better clarity to the public while better protecting the amphibians and reptiles. 
Poaching, harassment, increased collection pressure and wildlife trafficking are negatively 
impacting amphibian and reptile populations throughout North America and around the world. In 
addition, many emerging diseases are also causing increased pressure on amphibian and reptile 
populations

Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis  
For both of these rules, the state is not imposing additional costs above what is required in 
federal rules. If the federal changes were not promulgated in state administrative code, public 
water systems in Wisconsin would still be obligated to comply with these requirements under the 
federal Safe Drinking Water Act. There are no additional state costs of implementing and 
complying with the proposed state rule. The Economic Impact Analysis does provide an estimate 
of the costs of the federal rule requirements in Wisconsin. 
Implementing the federal and state rules for drinking water standards for PFAS (DG-01-24) will 
affect small businesses. These rules provide some flexibility by allowing monitoring waivers to 
reduce the frequency of required monitoring at public water systems that are below half of the 
MCL trigger levels of PFAS.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Fisheries Management

#### Public hearing on permanent rule relating to possession limits for various fish species, chs. NR 20 to 23

Start Date: 08/19/2026

End Date: 08/19/2026

Time: 2:00 p.m. - End of Agenda

Location: Virtual

Contact 

Kari Lee-Zimmerman, Kari.LeeZimmermann@wisconsin.gov or 608-316-0080

Details 

This is a public hearing on a proposed rule, Board Order FH-10-25, affecting chs. NR 20 to 23 and relating to possession limits for various fish species. This rule evaluates statewide fish possession limits and improves consistency in interpretation of possession limits between the boundary waters between Wisconsin and neighboring states and the inland and outlying waters. It also updates the description of possession limits so that it is clear that the possession limit for each specific species applies to all fish of that species harvested from all Wisconsin waterbodies collectively. The rule simplifies regulations by eliminating the total daily bag limit and allowance for the possession limit to be twice the daily bag limit. It clarifies that each waterbody has a daily bag limit and each species has a possession limit, and there are no other variances of those respective restrictions to confuse anglers.
